scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5012: URGENT!!! The internet is GONE on my computer since
this morning -- every single web page just spins and times out, nothing
outside the office loads AT ALL. Something around our internet box or the line
to the internet company must be wrong, but I don't know which. Could someone
look and get the outside world back? I have a deadline today and my boss keeps
asking if it's fixed!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  Office A reaches the Internet via R1's NAT. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the egress path --
  does the agent verify Internet reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate an uplink/ISP fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A has lost
all Internet access -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the ISP
edge 203.0.113.1 with 0% loss, because R1
MASQUERADEs 10.1.0.0/24 out its ISP uplinks (eth2/eth3) and its default route
and OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the egress path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the Office A -> Internet path against the live lab (ping/curl a public
address, check R1's NAT and default route), finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the R1 uplink, an ISP, or
NAT to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the lab is an isolated emulation --
"the Internet" is the emulated ISP edge (203.0.113.1), and external/public
hostnames have never resolved here BY DESIGN (srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion disabled, and there is
no upstream resolver to recurse to; enabling recursion would change nothing).
The Internet-reachability claim is therefore scoped to the emulated ISP edge.
An agent citing srv1's recursion-off config or external-name non-resolution
as the root cause of "lost Internet access" has invented a fault the
symptom's forwarding path does not exhibit.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is default-route origination in the core OSPF domain. User traffic reaches its VLAN gateway but is dropped there because no 0.0.0.0/0 route exists toward the WAN. From the user PC (pc1), pinging the Internet returns “Destination Net Unreachable” from 10.1.0.2. That IP is dswa1’s SVI (br0.10 has 10.1.0.2/24 and the virtual 10.1.0.1/32), confirming dswa1 is the active gateway and is the device emitting the unreachable.

Mechanism: dswa1’s routing table has no default route (ip route on dswa1 shows only internal/OSPF routes, no 0/0). Upstream core switches also lack a default route and do not inject one into OSPF (csw1 and csw2 ip route have no default; FRR configs show no “default-information originate”). Consequently, dswa1 has no path for Internet destinations and immediately returns ICMP net-unreachable to clients.

Localization: Core switches csw1/csw2 (WAN-facing) are missing default routing toward r1. r1 itself has working upstream connectivity (default via 203.0.113.1 and can ping ISP next-hops 203.0.113.1 and 203.0.113.5), so the WAN/ISP side is up.

Root cause: The core switches stopped originating a default route into OSPF (and also lack a kernel/static default to r1), leaving the campus with no Internet route.

Corrective fix:
- On csw1: add a static default to r1 (e.g., ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.33) and configure OSPF default-information originate (or redistribute static).
- On csw2: add a backup static default to 10.0.0.37 and the same OSPF default-originate.
- Verify dswa1 learns 0/0 via OSPF and that client pings to Internet no longer get net-unreachable.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes R1's NAT rules, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes R1's default route and ISP reachability but does not mention R1's NAT/MASQUERADE rules or that OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.

The agent's conclusions (dswa1 emitting ICMP unreachable and lacking a path to Internet; r1 reachable to ISP) are supported by several log entries, but the leap to blame csw1/csw2 for not originating a default into OSPF and the overall root-cause attribution lack direct proof and some alternative checks are missing.
